verses.zh: 大卫的儿子押沙龙有一个美貌的妹子，名叫她玛。大卫的儿子暗嫩爱她。
verses.en: Now David’s son Absalom[NOTE:1] had a beautiful sister named Tamar. In the course of time David’s son Amnon fell madly in love with her.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Amnon the son of David loved her.” The following verse indicates the extreme nature of his infatuation, so the translation uses “madly in love” here.sn Amnon was the half-brother of Tamar; Absalom was her full blood-brother.
Heb “and there was distress to Amnon so that he made himself sick.”

verses.zh: 暗嫩为他妹子她玛忧急成病。她玛还是处女，暗嫩以为难向她行事。
verses.en: But Amnon became frustrated because he was so lovesick[NOTE:1] over his sister Tamar. For she was a virgin, and to Amnon it seemed out of the question to do anything to her.
notes: Heb “and he said to him.”

verses.zh: 暗嫩有一个朋友，名叫约拿达，是大卫长兄示米亚的儿子。这约拿达为人极其狡猾；
verses.en: Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah. Jonadab was a very crafty man.

verses.zh: 他问暗嫩说：「王的儿子啊，为何一天比一天瘦弱呢？请你告诉我。」暗嫩回答说：「我爱我兄弟押沙龙的妹子她玛。」
verses.en: He asked Amnon,[NOTE:1] “Why are you, the king’s son,[NOTE:2] so depressed every morning? Can’t you tell me?” So Amnon said to him, “I’m in love with Tamar the sister of my brother Absalom.”
notes: A more idiomatic translation might be “Why are you of all people…?”

This verb is used in the Hitpael stem only in this chapter of the Hebrew Bible. With the exception of v. 2 it describes not a real sickness but one pretended in order to entrap Tamar. The Hitpael sometimes, as here, describes the subject making oneself appear to be of a certain character. On this use of the stem, see GKC 149-50 §54.e.

verses.zh: 约拿达说：「你不如躺在床上装病；你父亲来看你，就对他说：『求父叫我妹子她玛来，在我眼前预备食物，递给我吃，使我看见，好从她手里接过来吃。』」
verses.en: Jonadab replied to him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick.[NOTE:1] When your father comes in to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come in so she can fix some food for me. Let her prepare the food in my sight so I can watch. Then I will eat from her hand.’”
notes: Heb “in his sight.”

verses.zh: 于是暗嫩躺卧装病。王来看他，他对王说：「求父叫我妹子她玛来，在我眼前为我做两个饼，我好从她手里接过来吃。」
verses.en: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be sick. When the king came in to see him, Amnon said to the king, “Please let my sister Tamar come in so she can make a couple of cakes in my sight. Then I will eat from her hand.”

verses.zh: 大卫就打发人到宫里，对她玛说：「你往你哥哥暗嫩的屋里去，为他预备食物。」
verses.en: So David sent Tamar to the house saying, “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare some food for him.”

verses.zh: 她玛就到她哥哥暗嫩的屋里；暗嫩正躺卧。她玛抟面，在他眼前做饼，且烤熟了，
verses.en: So Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, who was lying down. She took the dough, kneaded it, made some cakes while he watched,[NOTE:1] and baked them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the cakes.”
Heb “from upon me.”

verses.zh: 在他面前将饼从锅里倒出来，他却不肯吃，便说：「众人离开我出去吧！」众人就都离开他，出去了。
verses.en: But when she took the pan and set it before him, he refused to eat. Instead Amnon said, “Get everyone out of here!”[NOTE:1] So everyone left.[NOTE:2]
notes: A few medieval Hebrew mss supported by the LXX and Vulgate read the Hiphil וַיּוֹצִיאוּ (vayyotsiʾu) “and they removed everyone,” rather than the MT’s Qal וַיֵּצְאוּ (vayyetseʾu, “they left”). This verb would then match the instructions more closely.
Heb “lie with me” (so NAB, NASB, NRSV); NCV “come and have sexual relations with me.”

verses.zh: 暗嫩对她玛说：「你把食物拿进卧房，我好从你手里接过来吃。」她玛就把所做的饼拿进卧房，到她哥哥暗嫩那里，
verses.en: Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the cakes into the bedroom; then I will eat from your hand.” So Tamar took the cakes that she had prepared and brought them to her brother Amnon in the bedroom.

verses.zh: 拿着饼上前给他吃，他便拉住她玛，说：「我妹妹，你来与我同寝。」
verses.en: As she brought them to him to eat, he grabbed her and said to her, “Come on! Get in bed with me,[NOTE:1] my sister!”
notes: Heb “and you will be like one of the fools.”

verses.zh: 她玛说：「我哥哥，不要玷辱我。以色列人中不当这样行，你不要做这丑事；
verses.en: But she said to him, “No, my brother! Don’t humiliate me! This just isn’t done in Israel! Don’t do this foolish thing!

verses.zh: 你玷辱了我，我何以掩盖我的羞耻呢？你在以色列中也成了愚妄人。你可以求王，他必不禁止我归你。」
verses.en: How could I ever be rid of my humiliation? And you would be considered one of the fools[NOTE:1] in Israel! Just[NOTE:2] speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.”
notes: Heb “Now.”
Heb “to her voice.”

verses.zh: 但暗嫩不肯听她的话，因比她力大，就玷辱她，与她同寝。
verses.en: But he refused to listen to her.[NOTE:1] He overpowered her and humiliated her by raping her.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and he humiliated her and lay with her.”
Heb “and Amnon hated her with very great hatred.”

verses.zh: 随后，暗嫩极其恨她，那恨她的心比先前爱她的心更甚，对她说：「你起来，去吧！」
verses.en: Then Amnon greatly despised her.[NOTE:1] His disdain toward her surpassed the love he had previously felt toward her.[NOTE:2] Amnon said to her, “Get up and leave!”
notes: Heb “for greater was the hatred with which he hated her than the love with which he loved her.”
Heb “No, because this great evil is [worse] than the other which you did with me, by sending me away.” Perhaps the broken syntax reflects her hysteria and outrage.

verses.zh: 她玛说：「不要这样！你赶出我去的这罪比你才行的更重！」但暗嫩不肯听她的话，
verses.en: But she said to him, “No I won’t, for sending me away now would be worse than what you did to me earlier!”[NOTE:1] But he refused to listen to her.
notes: Heb “send this [one] from upon me to the outside.”

verses.zh: 就叫伺候自己的仆人来，说：「将这个女子赶出去！她一出去，你就关门，上闩。」
verses.en: He called his personal attendant and said to him, “Take this woman out of my sight[NOTE:1] and lock the door behind her!”
notes: The Hebrew expression used here (כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים, ketonet passim) is found only here and in Gen 37:3, 23, 32. Hebrew פַּס (pas) can refer to the palm of the hand or the sole of the foot; here the idea is probably that of a long robe reaching to the feet and having sleeves reaching to the wrists. The notion of a “coat of many colors” (KJV, ASV “garment of divers colors”), a familiar translation for the phrase in Genesis, is based primarily on the translation adopted in the LXX χιτῶνα ποικίλον (chitōna poikilon) and does not have a great deal of support.

verses.zh: 那时她玛穿着彩衣，因为没有出嫁的公主都是这样穿。暗嫩的仆人就把她赶出去，关门上闩。
verses.en: (Now she was wearing a long robe,[NOTE:1] for this is what the king’s virgin daughters used to wear.) So Amnon’s[NOTE:2] attendant removed her and bolted the door[NOTE:3] behind her.
notes: Heb “his”; the referent (Amnon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The Hebrew verb is a perfect with nonconsecutive vav, probably indicating an action (locking the door) that complements the preceding one (pushing her out the door).

Heb “Don’t set your heart to this thing!” Elsewhere this phrase means to disregard or not pay attention to something (e.g. Exod 7:23). It is a callous thing to say to Tamar, but to the degree that what he said becomes known, it misleads people from understanding that he is personally plotting revenge (13:22, 28).

verses.zh: 她玛把灰尘撒在头上，撕裂所穿的彩衣，以手抱头，一面行走，一面哭喊。
verses.en: Then Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the long robe she was wearing. She put her hands on her head and went on her way, wailing as she went.

verses.zh: 她胞兄押沙龙问她说：「莫非你哥哥暗嫩与你亲近了吗？我妹妹，暂且不要作声，他是你的哥哥，不要将这事放在心上。」她玛就孤孤单单地住在她胞兄押沙龙家里。
verses.en: Her brother Absalom said to her, “Was Amnon your brother with you? Now be quiet, my sister. He is your brother. Don’t take it so seriously!”[NOTE:1] Tamar, devastated, lived in the house of her brother Absalom.
notes: The LXX and part of the Old Latin tradition include the following addition to v. 21, also included in some English versions (e.g., NAB, NRSV, CEV): “But he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, since he was his firstborn.” Note David’s attitude toward his son Adonijah in 1 Kgs 1:6.

verses.zh: 大卫王听见这事，就甚发怒。
verses.en: Now King David heard about all these things and was very angry.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map1-D2; Map2-D3; Map3-A2; Map4-C1.

verses.zh: 押沙龙并不和他哥哥暗嫩说好说歹；因为暗嫩玷辱他妹妹她玛，所以押沙龙恨恶他。
verses.en: But Absalom said nothing to Amnon, either bad or good, yet Absalom hated Amnon because he had humiliated his sister Tamar.

verses.zh: 过了二年，在靠近以法莲的巴力・夏琐有人为押沙龙剪羊毛；押沙龙请王的众子与他同去。
verses.en: Two years later Absalom’s sheepshearers were in Baal Hazor,[NOTE:1] near Ephraim. Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
notes: Heb “your servant has sheepshearers.” The phrase “your servant” also occurs at the end of the verse and is translated as "me".

verses.zh: 押沙龙来见王，说：「现在有人为仆人剪羊毛，请王和王的臣仆与仆人同去。」
verses.en: Then Absalom went to the king and said, “My shearers have begun their work.[NOTE:1] Let the king and his servants go with me.”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Absalom) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 王对押沙龙说：「我儿，我们不必都去，恐怕使你耗费太多。」押沙龙再三请王，王仍是不肯去，只为他祝福。
verses.en: But the king said to Absalom, “No, my son. We shouldn’t all go. We shouldn’t burden you in that way.” Though Absalom[NOTE:1] pressed[NOTE:2] him, the king[NOTE:3] was not willing to go. Instead, David[NOTE:4] blessed him.
notes: Here and in v. 27 the translation follows 4QSama ויפצר (vayyiftsar, “and he pressed”) rather than the MT וַיִּפְרָץ (vayyifrats, “and he broke through”). This emended reading seems also to underlie the translations of the LXX (καὶ ἐβιάσατο, kai ebiasato), the Syriac Peshitta (weʾalseh), and Vulgate (cogeret eum).
Heb “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and not.”

verses.zh: 押沙龙说：「王若不去，求王许我哥哥暗嫩同去。」王说：「何必要他去呢？」
verses.en: Then Absalom said, “If you will not go,[NOTE:1] then let my brother Amnon go with us.” The king replied to him, “Why should he go with you?”
notes: Heb “when good is the heart of Amnon with wine.”

verses.zh: 押沙龙再三求王，王就许暗嫩和王的众子与他同去。
verses.en: But when Absalom pressed him, he sent Amnon and all the king’s sons along with him.

verses.zh: 押沙龙吩咐仆人说：「你们注意，看暗嫩饮酒畅快的时候，我对你们说杀暗嫩，你们便杀他，不要惧怕。这不是我吩咐你们的吗？你们只管壮胆奋勇！」
verses.en: Absalom instructed his servants, “Look! When Amnon is drunk[NOTE:1] and I say to you, ‘Strike Amnon down,’ kill him then and there. Don’t fear! Is it not I who have given you these instructions? Be strong and courageous!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and become sons of valor.”
Heb “it was placed on the mouth of Absalom.”

verses.zh: 押沙龙的仆人就照押沙龙所吩咐的，向暗嫩行了。王的众子都起来，各人骑上骡子，逃跑了。
verses.en: So Absalom’s servants did to Amnon exactly what Absalom had instructed. Then all the king’s sons got up; each one rode away on his mule and fled.

verses.zh: 他们还在路上，有风声传到大卫那里，说：「押沙龙将王的众子都杀了，没有留下一个。」
verses.en: While they were still on their way, the following report reached David: “Absalom has killed all the king’s sons; not one of them is left!”

verses.zh: 王就起来，撕裂衣服，躺在地上。王的臣仆也都撕裂衣服，站在旁边。
verses.en: Then the king stood up and tore his garments and lay down on the ground. All his servants were standing there with torn garments as well.

verses.zh: 大卫的长兄，示米亚的儿子约拿达说：「我主，不要以为王的众子―少年人都杀了，只有暗嫩一个人死了。自从暗嫩玷辱押沙龙妹子她玛的那日，押沙龙就定意杀暗嫩了。
verses.en: Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah, said, “My lord should not say, ‘They have killed all the young men who are the king’s sons.’ For only Amnon is dead. This is what Absalom has talked about[NOTE:1] from the day that Amnon[NOTE:2] humiliated his sister Tamar.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Amnon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “behind him.”

verses.zh: 现在，我主我王，不要把这事放在心上，以为王的众子都死了，只有暗嫩一个人死了。」
verses.en: Now don’t let my lord the king be concerned about the report that has come saying, ‘All the king’s sons are dead.’ It is only Amnon who is dead.”

verses.zh: 押沙龙逃跑了。守望的少年人举目观看，见有许多人从山坡的路上来。
verses.en: In the meantime Absalom fled. When the servant who was the watchman looked up, he saw many people coming from the west[NOTE:1] on a road beside the hill.
notes: Heb “and they lifted their voice and wept.”

verses.zh: 约拿达对王说：「看哪，王的众子都来了，果然与你仆人所说的相合。」
verses.en: Jonadab said to the king, “Look! The king’s sons have come! It’s just as I said.”

verses.zh: 话才说完，王的众子都到了，放声大哭；王和臣仆也都哭得甚恸。
verses.en: Just as he finished speaking, the king’s sons arrived, wailing and weeping.[NOTE:1] The king and all his servants wept loudly[NOTE:2] as well.
notes: Heb “with a great weeping.”
The Hebrew text leaves the word “David” to be inferred. The Syriac Peshitta and Vulgate add the word “David.” Most of the Greek tradition includes the words “King David” here.

verses.zh: 押沙龙逃到基述王亚米忽的儿子达买那里去了。大卫天天为他儿子悲哀。
verses.en: But Absalom fled and went to King Talmai son of Ammihud of Geshur. And David[NOTE:1] grieved over his son every day.
notes: The translation follows 4QSama in reading רוּחַ הַמֶּלֶךְ (ruakh hammelekh, “the spirit of the king”) rather than the MT דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ (david hammelekh, “David the king”). The understanding reflected in the translation above is that David, though alienated during this time from his son Absalom, still had an abiding love and concern for him. He longed for reconciliation with him. A rather different interpretation of the verse supposes that David’s interest in taking military action against Absalom grew slack with the passing of time, and this in turn enabled David’s advisers to encourage him toward reconciliation with Absalom. For the latter view, see P. K. McCarter, II Samuel (AB), 344, and cf. CEV.

verses.zh: 押沙龙逃到基述，在那里住了三年。
verses.en: After Absalom fled and went to Geshur, he remained there for three years.

verses.zh: 暗嫩死了以后，大卫王得了安慰，心里切切想念押沙龙。
verses.en: The king longed[NOTE:1] to go to Absalom, for he had since been consoled over the death of Amnon.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “was consoled over Amnon because he was dead.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter is a sad fulfillment of 2 Sam. 12:10-12.

- David's family became cursed with sexual sins.

- Amnon and Tamar (cf. 2 Samuel 13; the Jewish Study Bible, p. 640, says "Tamar's rape is seen as punishment for David,
corresponding to his adultery").

- Absalom and David's concubines (cf. 2 Sam. 15:16; 16:21-22)

- Solomon in his old age and his pagan wives (cf. 1 Kgs. 11:1-8)

- This chapter clearly illustrates the difference between love and lust.

- The Jewish Study Bible, p. 641, says

"Absalom murders Amnon to avenge his sister's rape. The murder is a punishment not only for Amnon,
but also for David for his murder of Uriah."

- This episode is omitted in Chronicles, as are most of the negative things related to David and his reign.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 13:1-6

1Now it was after this that Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister whose name
was Tamar, and Amnon the son of David loved her. 2Amnon was so frustrated because
of his sister Tamar that he made himself ill, for she was a virgin, and it seemed hard to Amnon to do
anything to her. 3But Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah,
David's brother; and Jonadab was a very shrewd man. 4He said to him, "O son of the king,
why are you so depressed morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" Then Amnon said to him,
"I am in love with Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom." 5Jonadab then said to him,
"Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill; when your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Please
let my sister Tamar come and give me some food to eat, and let her prepare the food in my sight, that
I may see it and eat from her hand.'" 6So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill; when
the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, "Please let my sister Tamar come and make me a
couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand."

13:1 "Absalom" He was the third oldest son of David.

- Amnon ‒ 2 Sam. 3:2

- Chileab ‒ 2 Sam. 3:3 (called Daniel in 1 Chr. 3:2, who must have died early)

- Absalom ‒ 2 Sam. 3:3

- Adonijah ‒ 2 Sam. 3:4

David's sin affected all of these children.

▣ "Tamar" This name (BDB 1071 II; NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 308-309) means "date palm." OT women were
often named after trees. The date palm's silhouette looked like a woman's form (cf. Song of Songs 7:7).

Notice the dramatic swing from

- love (BDB 12, KB 17) in vv. 1,4,15 (twice)

- hate (BDB 971, KB 1338) in v. 15 (twice)

13:2

NASB
"frustrated"

NKJV
"distressed"

NRSV, REB, LXX
"tormented"

NJB
"obsessed"

JPSOA
"distraught"

Peshitta
"much grieved"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 864 I. B., KB 1058; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 854, #1),
which literally means "to bind," "to tie up," or "to be restricted." Emotionally he was in a cramped place. He could not
think of anything else (NJB). The text does not mention if he was married but being the first in line for the throne,
probably he was.

▣ "she was a virgin" This term (BDB 143) is used to show

- she was of marriageable age

- she was strictly guarded by palace servants and was not allowed any private contact with a man, even her half-brother
(Josephus, Antiq. 7.8.1)

- this heightens David's poor decision to order her to go to Amnon's house (v. 7; apparently all the kings sons had their
own residences)

13:3

NASB, TEV, NJB, REB
"very shrewd man"

NKJV, NRSV
"very crafty man"

JPSOA
"very clever man"

Peshitta
"very wise man"

The ADJECTIVE "shrewd" (BDB 314, #3) denotes a wisdom or skill, but in some
contexts it is a skill toward evil or trickery (i.e., 2 Sam. 14:2; Job 5:13).

13:4 "O son of the king" He was one of several sons but he was the firstborn and was, therefore, in line for
the throne. He had a special standing which came with special privileges and power.

13:5-6 What a sad piece of advice! What a tragedy! Maybe Jonadab expected Amnon to marry her.

13:6 "cakes" This root (BDB 525, KB 516 II; NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 519-521) is found only in this chapter.
It could refer to pancakes or dumplings (AB). It was food for a sick person.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 13:7-14

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- In this period could a brother marry his half-sister?

- Why is Amnon's action so horrendous?

- Did Jonadab expect Amnon to marry Tamar?

- List the three reasons Tamar gives why Amnon should not violate her.

- List the signs of mourning in vv. 19,31.

- Did Absalom act

- for his sister's honor

- to gain the throne

- both

- Why did Absalom flee to Geshur?
